text:
Sophia: quick sync post-rfc triage. I'm worried our current adapter handshake is trying to be 'too smart' - it leaks autoscale/node layout and forces adapter churn. propose we shrink the required surface to a tiny set: identity, capability_flags, probe, and a creds TTL. keep everything else opaque.
Raj: I like the promise of lean. how do we communicate eviction/drain state? ops needs a way to avoid routing to nodes being drained.
Mei: add a short-lived 'state' code returned by probe. e.g. 204=ready, 202=draining, 409=migration-required, 5xx=transient. router treats 202 as soft-exclude for new requests but allows in-flight to finish.
Tom: important: draining must be cheap to evaluate on on-prem. please avoid probes that run heavy cache compactions. make a separate shallow /_handshake endpoint.
Sophia: agreed. handshake rules: - probe must be idempotent and <10ms typical; - probe codes as Mei said; - creds_expires_at ISO8601 timestamp; - capability_flags is a list of short tokens (kv_v2, quant, fast_attn).
Raj: what about SLO hints? we sometimes need latency-aware routing (sync vs async).
Mei: allow advisory_slo object but mark advisory. control plane must never rely on it for correctness. router can prefer p50/p95 hints when present for sync routes.
Tom: also want a minimal 'compat_version' string for model-serving ABI, so we can do quick compatibility checks before routing. e.g., compat_v=2.1.
Sophia: fine. keep compat_version name short. manifest example: 
```
{
  "identity": "tenant-42/adapter-a",
  "compat_version": "2.1",
  "capability_flags": ["kv_v2","quant","stream-chunked"],
  "probe_endpoint": "/_handshake",
  "credentials_expires_at": "2026-05-01T12:00:00Z",
  "advisory_slo": {"p50_ms":"35","p95_ms":"120"},
  "quirks_note": "air_gapped=false; local_kms=true"
}
```
Raj: small question: 'quirks_note' should be free-form and only human readable, not parsed by control plane. we need an alternate channel for machine-readable ops hooks if needed.
Mei: yes, add opaque_metadata_uri optional field where adapter can put a signed blob or URL reachable only by infra - RFC will define access. control plane won't parse it.
Tom: migration semantics: when probe returns 409, router should attempt failover to a compatible-variant. define compatible-variant as matching capability_flags superset/compatible and compat_version within same major. exact matching rules live in control plane policy.
Sophia: we should document that capability flags are feature flags, not policies. routers evaluate them against policy. don't bake policies into manifests.
infra-bot: handshake-check: schema:v1 quick-validate passed for hosted/dedicated adapters, private returned advisory warnings (quirks_note present).
Raj: testing plan: unit tests for parser + probe semantics, plus a compatibility sweep across adapters to ensure flags cover common combos. I'll own the sweep.
Mei: ops runbook items: add probe codes, draining behavior, creds refresh workflow (watch credentials_expires_at and surface alert at T-10m).
Tom: tiny implementation note: make probe expensive-path opt-in behind /_handshake?detailed=true so ops can run deeper health checks without affecting router. default probe must be shallow.
Sophia: next steps: I'll write the one-pager and minimal JSON schema and add an example adapter harness test. Raj will run sweep and Tom will prototype shallow handshake endpoint.
Raj: will do. if handshake stays tiny we avoid repeated adapter updates across hosted/dedicated/private. :thumbsup:
Mei: thanks all. we can tighten rules in RFC but this gives a practical guardrail: lean required fields, probe-first semantics, advisory hints only, opaque metadata for infra.
